questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-02 bilateral breakthrough signal toward Oman (Al Jazeera, AFP/Straits Times, Hindustan Times, Khaleej Times): hours after US President Donald Trump cancelled planned large-scale US-Israeli attacks on Iran (citing Saudi Crown Prince MBS's intervention and claiming 'deal perimeters' for opening the Strait of Hormuz), Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reported to the cabinet on Sunday Aug 2 that Tehran-Muscat negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz have entered their 'final stages' and are 'on the way to being finalised.' Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei simultaneously told state TV that Iran and Oman are close to an understanding on a new maritime corridor through Hormuz (distinct from prior northern/southern routes) safeguarding both states' sovereignty and security, reversing the July 29-31 breakdown when Iran rejected Oman's earlier proposal. Lifting Oman sharply (0.41 -> 0.54) as the co-littoral state actively finalizing a bilateral Hormuz corridor framework with Tehran, while capping below 0.55 because Muscat has not yet publicly confirmed, Baghaei noted the route deal does not itself reopen the strait, and a dedicated sea-mine clearance project has not yet been formally announced—leaving meaningful probability that a naval minehunter-equipped mediator/partner such as China (0.20 -> 0.16), Pakistan (0.17 -> 0.15; lawmaker Ghashghavi cited active mediation to revive the June Islamabad MoU and Araghchi spoke with army chief Asim Munir last week), Russia (0.08 -> 0.06), Turkey (0.03 -> 0.02), or another country (7% residual including Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, India, France) signs the demining agreement.

questions.title: Which club will Mohamed Salah join first after leaving Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season?
questions.background: Mohamed Salah has announced that he will leave Liverpool at the end of the season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Salah or his new club, or reliable news reporting confirming a completed signing. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first club with which Salah signs a senior playing contract following his departure from Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season. Transfer speculation, negotiations, and trial appearances do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club.
questions.current_reasoning: Major August 2 transfer swing toward Trabzonspor across multiple independent outlets: ESPN (Aug 2, 09:08 AM) and Foot Mercato report Trabzonspor are in pole position after significant progress with Salah's camp while rivals Besiktas suspended talks (refusing to raise their offer despite a prior verbal agreement); Ajel (Aug 2) cites Turkish journalist Yagiz Sabuncuoglu that Trabzonspor offered a 2-year EUR 17M/yr deal plus 20-25% shirt-sales share; and Milliyet (Aug 2, 21:40 TRT) reports talks with Ramy Abbas are in the final stages targeting an Aug 5 arrival, with coach Fatih Tekke notably declining to deny negotiations after the Udinese friendly ('I cannot say anything because it has not become official yet') while management seeks sponsor backing. However, Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan publicly denied an agreement on A Spor and at the club's anniversary event (ESPN, Aug 2, 10:29 AM ET), and Turkish media note sponsorship funding is still being arranged. Meanwhile, Jarayid (Aug 1) cited Al-Ittihad sources confirming talks remain only exploratory with no deal agreed. Moving Trabzonspor to clear favorite (0.15 -> 0.48, capped below 0.50 because the deal is unconfirmed and publicly denied by the club president), cutting Al-Ittihad (0.37 -> 0.20), lifting Besiktas slightly as a Turkish fallback (0.07 -> 0.09), and trimming Al-Qadsiah (0.10 -> 0.06) and Sporting Kansas City (0.12 -> 0.05), leaving 12% residual.

questions.title: What sentence will Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa receive at trial in her drug-trafficking case?
questions.background: Sarah Khalifa was arrested in Egypt in April 2025 as part of a drug investigation.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The trial court’s announced judgment in the drug-trafficking prosecution stemming from Khalifa’s April 2025 arrest, as confirmed by official court information or reliable reporting from Al-Ahram. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the trial court announces its verdict and sentence. Later appellate decisions and judgments in unrelated cases do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide a short legal term identifying the principal penalty imposed, or the court’s disposition if no penalty is imposed. If multiple penalties are imposed, report the most severe.
questions.current_reasoning: Major procedural and legal update from July 8-9 Arabic court reporting (Al-Ahram, Masrawy, Al-Ain, Newsroom): on July 9, the New Cairo Criminal Court adjourned the trial of Sarah Khalifa and 27 co-defendants directly to August 4, 2026 WITHOUT referring the case papers to the Grand Mufti. Under Article 381(2) of Egypt's Code of Criminal Procedure, a criminal court cannot pronounce a death sentence without first referring the file to the Grand Mufti and adjourning weeks later for final sentencing—meaning a death sentence cannot legally be handed down on August 4. Substantively, two further disclosures weaken capital sentencing: (1) Masrawy's indictment summary confirms Khalifa is Defendant #4 (financier/coordinator, plus personal drug-use and unlicensed firearms charges), behind fugitive ringleaders #1 and #2; and (2) defense counsel invoked a Supreme Constitutional Court ruling invalidating scheduling decrees by the Head of the Egyptian Drug Authority. However, the 3-member forensic committee and forensic expert testified on July 8-9 that 2018-2019 Minister of Health decrees explicitly schedule narcotics 'analogues' and confirmed the lab analysis was technically sound, while the court firmly rejected defense procedural challenges. Accordingly, cutting Death penalty sharply 0.28 -> 0.06 (retaining 6% only if the court issues a Mufti referral on Aug 4 for a later verdict), lifting Life imprisonment 0.46 -> 0.56 as the primary statutory penalty under Narcotics Law Art. 33, raising Aggravated imprisonment 0.13 -> 0.19 (Art. 17 clemency or lesser trafficking/firearms counts), Acquittal 0.07 -> 0.11 (Constitutional Court scheduling defense), and Imprisonment 0.04 -> 0.06 (conviction only on drug use/minor counts), with 2% residual.

questions.title: Who will win the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Kansas in 2026?
questions.background: Kansas will hold a U.S. Senate election in November 2026, with party nominees selected in the August primary.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results reported by Kansas election authorities or definitive election reporting from a major news organization. Resolution : Resolve to the winner of Kansas's Democratic U.S. Senate primary scheduled for August 4, 2026, once the outcome is unambiguously reported. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Late-stage establishment consolidation ahead of the August 4 Kansas Democratic Senate primary: on July 30, the Kansas City Star Editorial Board—covering Kansas's largest Democratic primary electorate in the KC/Johnson County metro—unanimously and enthusiastically endorsed Adam Hamilton, following July 28 Topeka Capital-Journal coverage of former Gov. Kathleen Sebelius actively campaigning with Hamilton in Topeka (rival Patrick Schmidt's home district). With mail/early voting underway, 3 days remaining, no rival polling surge or consolidation across the fractured 11-candidate field, a commanding +17 mid-July GBAO poll lead (30%-13%-10%-5%-2%), and >20x fundraising dominance ($3.66M), raising Adam Hamilton 0.89 -> 0.92 while retaining an 8% upset buffer across Christy Davis (0.04), Noah Taylor (0.02), Patrick Schmidt (0.01), Erik Murray (0.005), and 0.5% for the remaining field.

questions.title: Which prominent RSF field commander will Darfur's governor announce has been killed in western Sudan in early August 2026?
questions.background: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) are a paramilitary group fighting Sudan's army in a war that began in April 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the RSF field commander whose death in fighting in western Sudan Darfur Governor Minni Arko Minnawi announces during August 1–10, 2026, according to Al Jazeera's reporting. The question concerns the governor's announcement, not independent confirmation of the death. Resolution Date : 2026-08-10 (announcement window: August 1–10, 2026) Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the commander's name, omitting military rank and nickname.
questions.current_reasoning: Key June 30 Africa Defense Forum confirmation (citing Asharq Al-Awsat): former RSF commander Ali 'Al-Safna' Rizqallah defected to the Sudanese Armed Forces in May 2026 (alongside April defector Al-Nour al-Qubba) and received an SAF rank, eliminating Ali Rizqallah (previously 0.07) as an active RSF commander. Meanwhile, on July 26-27 (Al Jazeera, Radio Dabanga, AFP), SAF and Darfur Governor Minni Arko Minnawi's Joint Force launched a major North Kordofan offensive seizing Bara, Jabra El Sheikh, and parts of the Khartoum-El Obeid Export Road as Hemedti ordered frontline reinforcements. Replacing Ali Rizqallah with UNSC-sanctioned RSF Chief of Operations Osman Mohamed Hamid (0.07), aligning Barkallah's spelling to Al Jazeera's exact July 14 reporting ('Abdul Rahman Juma Barkallah'), and retaining a calibrated 56% residual outside the top 5 for other active RSF Darfur/Kordofan field commanders.

questions.title: Which university will house Raja Shehadeh's personal diary archive by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: Raja Shehadeh is a Palestinian writer and lawyer who has kept personal diaries since 1967.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the university confirmed to be physically holding Shehadeh's original personal diary archive by August 31, 2026. Confirmation must come from public statements by Shehadeh or the receiving university, or contemporaneous news reporting establishing that the archive has arrived, rather than merely announcing a planned transfer. Resolution Date : 2026-08-31 Accepted Answer Format : string (institution). Answer with the university's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Palestinian writer and lawyer Raja Shehadeh (turning 75 in July 2026) has kept personal diaries in Ramallah since 1967, and no confirmed university deposit has been announced as of June 24, 2026. The strongest institutional fits are the University of Oxford (whose St Antony's Middle East Centre Archive and Bodleian Library are premier safe UK repositories for Palestinian papers, aligning with Shehadeh's London legal training, UK publisher Profile Books, and Orwell Prize ties), Birzeit University (his local Ramallah alma mater where his wife Penny Johnson is a researcher), the American University of Beirut (his BA alma mater with major Palestinian archival holdings), Columbia University (home to Edward Said's papers), and SOAS University of London. Because dozens of UK, US, and Middle Eastern universities could plausibly acquire the archive, 49% probability mass is left outside the top five.
